title: Arancini al Ragù
subtitle: Sicilian fried rice balls with beef and pea filling
excerpt: Golden fried rice balls filled with slow-cooked beef ragù and peas, coated in breadcrumbs and deep-fried until crisp. The great street food of Palermo, made from leftover risotto or specially made saffron-scented rice.

recipe.sourceNotes: Arancini, the name means little oranges in Sicilian dialect, referring to their shape and colour, are the defining street food of Sicily, particularly Palermo and Catania. Their origins are traced to the Arab-Norman period of Sicilian history in the tenth and eleventh centuries, when saffron rice was a staple food. The filling varies by region: ragù and peas in Palermo, butter and béchamel in Catania.

recipeTools.notes: Deep pan for frying, or deep-fat fryer.

content.text: Arancini are a project, not a weeknight dinner, but they are worth it. The rice base needs to be cold before you shape them, warm rice will not hold together. Make the rice and ragù filling the day before, then shape and fry on the day. Once shaped, they can be coated and refrigerated for several hours before frying. The key to the coating is double-coating: rice, then flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.

Make the rice: bring the stock to a simmer. Add the rice and cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the stock is absorbed and the rice is cooked through, 18 to 20 minutes. Stir in the saffron water, butter, parmesan, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Spread on a tray and cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Make the ragù filling: fry the onion in olive oil for 6 minutes. Add the mince and brown well. Add the tomato puree for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and 50 ml water. Season and simmer for 20 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas and cook for 3 minutes. Cool completely.

Shape the arancini: wet your hands. Take a handful of cold rice (about 80 g), flatten it in your palm, place a tablespoon of ragù filling in the centre, and close the rice around it, pressing firmly to form a ball. Place on a tray. Repeat with the remaining rice and filling.
Coat each ball: dust in flour, dip in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs, pressing firmly. For a thicker coating, dip in egg and breadcrumbs a second time. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to firm up.
Heat the oil to 170 C in a deep pan. Fry the arancini in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper and serve immediately.
